Opens the graphics window and has to be called before any drawing command. Calling it again closes the window and opens a new one, and then all images and textures are gone, so load them again. It also puts the colors and the current buffer back to their defaults.

```blitzbasic
;media still display/graphics.png
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Cls
Text 160, 100, "Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2", 1, 1
Text 160, 120, "Width " + GraphicsWidth() + ", Height " + GraphicsHeight(), 1, 1
Flip
WaitKey
```

![Graphics](media/display/graphics.png)
## Color depth

The `depth` argument is not a display mode: it picks what the buffers are made of, so that many faint layers drawn over each other do not lose their small steps to rounding. The window always shows 8 bits per channel.

| Depth | Buffer |
|---|---|
| 0 | Same as 32. |
| 8 | A palette of 256 colors, set with [GraphicsPalette](GraphicsPalette). |
| 12 | R4G4B4A4. |
| 15 | A1R5G5B5. |
| 16 | R5G6B5, no alpha. |
| 24 | R8G8B8, no alpha. |
| 30 | R10G10B10A2. |
| 32 | R8G8B8A8. |
| 64 | R16G16B16A16 as half precision floats (values above 1 are kept). |

Any other number gives 32 with a warning. If the graphics card can't draw to a format, the next smaller one in the table is used and a warning says so; [GraphicsDepth](GraphicsDepth) tells you which you got. [GfxModeDepth](GfxModeDepth), `DisplayDepth` and `DisplayModeDepth` always say 32, and `WBuffer` does nothing.

Pixel commands (`ReadPixel`, `WritePixel`, the `Fast` and `CopyPixel` versions) take and give ARGB with 8 bits per channel for every depth, except 30, which uses A2R10G10B10. Depths 8, 12, 15 and 16 are widened to 8 bits per channel, and what you write is rounded to the nearest value the buffer can hold. For depth 64, [ReadPixel64](ReadPixel64) and [WritePixel64](WritePixel64) work with the half float channels as they are. Textures and images are always RGBA8, and `SaveBuffer`, `GrabImage` and `CopyRect` convert on the way.

[Dither](Dither) adds noise of one step of the buffer before rounding, which hides banding. The same scene with the depths 32, 16, 15, 12 and 8, without and with Dither:

![A lit sphere and two gradients with the depths 32, 16, 15, 12 and 8 from top to bottom, without Dither (left) and with Dither (right)](media/graphics/color-depth-low.png)

Depth 30 or 64 matters most for soft mist or smoke made of many overlapping, nearly transparent sprites: with 8 bits every blend rounds, and contour lines show where a faint layer changes nothing. Depth 30 stayed within half a step of the exact result in tests, so it is the first choice for such scenes. Dither does not help in a depth 32 buffer, because it dithers before the blend rounds again.

![The same 16 columns of 100 faint layers drawn with the depths 32, 24, 30 and 64, from top to bottom](media/graphics/color-depth-ramp.png)

@param width   Width of the picture in pixels.
@param height  Height of the picture in pixels.
@param depth   Color depth in bits, see Color depth above: 8, 12, 15, 16, 24, 30, 32 or 64, or 0 for 32. Defaults to 0.
@param mode    0 opens a window, 1 uses full screen (a borderless window over the display, see [Fullscreen](Fullscreen)), 2 opens a window and 3 opens a window that the user can resize. 4 opens a window without a border: no title bar and no frame. Mode 4 is a BlitzLLVM extension that original Blitz does not have. Defaults to 0.
@gap `Graphics` is the same command as [Graphics3D](Graphics3D): there is no 2D-only mode, so the 3D commands work after `Graphics` as well.
@gap The depth picks the format of the buffers and not a display mode, and the 8 bit mode has a palette. See Color depth above.
@gap Full screen (mode 1) does not change the video mode of the display: the picture is shown at the largest size that fits with its aspect ratio kept, and the rest is black. See [Fullscreen](Fullscreen).
@gap In a resizable window (mode 3) the picture is scaled to the size of the window, and the mouse position is converted to picture pixels.
@gap The modes 6 and 7 of Blitz3D, which pause the program while the window is in the background, act like 2 and 3. The program keeps running.
@gap A window without a border (mode 4) has the size you ask for and cannot be resized by the user.
@gap A width or height below 1 stops the program with an error message.
